Not an Xbox disc image, or no default.xbe in it: %1$s

This folder\'s default.xbe is not the game this app was made for (another game, or another region). Choose the right game in Game data.

This app runs a recompiled Xbox game on Android. The game itself is not included: you bring your own copy, from a disc you own. Setting it up takes a minute, or a few for a disc image.
The folder of your extracted disc, or a disc image (.iso)
The app checks it is the right game, and copies or extracts it if needed
Settings and game data stay one press away
Use a game you own: the folder of your extracted disc, or a disc image you made yourself. Your current game stays until the new one has been checked.
The extracted disc: default.xbe and its files, on the device or an SD card. Read in place with All files access, otherwise copied into the app.
A .iso or .xiso image of your disc. Extracted once into the app\'s storage: it needs the game\'s size free and takes a few minutes.

With « All files access », the app reads the game straight from the folder you choose, on the phone or on an SD card: no copy, and it works for a 4 GB disc. The app only reads the game folder you pick.\n\nWithout it, the folder is copied into the app\'s own storage: that takes as much free space again and a few minutes, and the copy is removed with the app.
Opens the system page: turn it on for this app, come back, then pick the folder.
No permission. The folder is copied into the app\'s storage: as much free space again, a few minutes; removed with the app.
Your current game is kept until the new one has been checked. Keep the app open until the end.
Stop and keep the current game
The game is already running: Play brings it back where you left it.
Saved in %1$s and applied the next time the game starts. Lines you add there yourself are kept.
Open the game directly next time
Next time, the game opens directly. Long-press the app icon › Launcher to come back here.
Next time, this screen shows first.
The console language the game sees

The language the Xbox tells the game. The game shows its menus, text and voices in it when its disc has that language (a European disc usually does, a US disc is often English only); otherwise the game picks one itself, usually English. « Same as Android » follows the phone\'s language. A game can have its own in the in-game menu (Quick settings). Applies the next time the game starts. (RECOMP_LANGUAGE)
Skip this screen when the game is ready
On: the app icon starts the game straight away when it is set up. Off: this screen shows first, with Play selected.
Long-press the app icon › Launcher (or Change game) to reach this screen while it is on.
Saved at once; applied the next time the game starts.
Saved. Applied the next time the game starts.
Saved. The game is running: it uses the new setting after it is restarted.
The game is running: changes apply the next time it starts.
Lines you wrote in recomp.cfg yourself are kept
Puts every option on this screen back to its default, by removing its lines from recomp.cfg. Other lines in the file are left as they are.
Defaults restored. Applied the next time the game starts.
Show each frame in step with the screen
On: frames are shown in step with the display, without tearing. Off: frames are shown as soon as they are ready; a little less delay, but the picture can tear. (RECOMP_PRESENT_VSYNC)
Draw on the CPU or on the GPU (experimental)

Software: the game is drawn by the CPU, the tested path. GPU: drawn with OpenGL ES, much faster in menus; still experimental, some effects may be missing or wrong. Auto: what this game\'s profile chooses (software for now). If the GPU cannot start, the game falls back to software. (RECOMP_GPU)
Frames per second at most, to save battery

With the GPU renderer, menus and pause screens can run at 200 frames per second or more, which only drains the battery and heats the device. The cap holds them to 60 (or 30). Auto: what this game\'s profile chooses (60, or 30 where the profile asks for even pacing, as Fable does). Off removes it, for testing. No effect with the software renderer. (RECOMP_GPU_FPS_CAP)
How textures are sampled when drawn

Sharp takes the nearest texel, as the game is drawn by default. Smooth blends four texels; anisotropic also follows surfaces seen at an angle. Smoother modes cost speed, and are not the default because they change the look the game was tested with. (RECOMP_TEX_BILINEAR, RECOMP_TEX_ANISO)
On: sounds the game places in 3D are filtered to sound like they come from their direction, best with headphones. Off: plain stereo panning. (RECOMP_APU_HRTF)

The size of each buffer handed to the device, in samples (256, 512, 1024, 2048). Short: less delay between the picture and the sound. Long: fewer crackles and drop-outs on a busy device. (RECOMP_AUDIO_BUF_SAMPLES)

Threads of the software renderer that share large triangles and vertex shading. Auto uses every core the game runs on but one (the fast cores when "Fast cores only" is on). More can be faster on a big SoC; fewer can help when the game itself is short of cores. (RECOMP_RASTER_THREADS)
Keep the game on the big cores
On: the game runs on the SoC\'s fast cores only, as set at start. Off: the system may also put it on the slow cores; try it only if the game stutters with this on. (RECOMP_BIG_CORES)
For bug reports: checks in the log

Runs the runtime\'s self-test before the game starts and writes one PASS or FAIL line per check to the log (logcat, tag xboxrecomp). Useful in a bug report; the game then starts as usual. (RECOMP_SHELL_SELFTEST)
Another folder or disc image, or import again
Pick a game folder or a disc image. The current game stays until the new one has been checked; a running game is closed then. Saves are kept.
Free the space; saves are kept
Removes %1$s, the copy this app made. Your saves stay (internal storage). You then choose the game again to play.
Press A again within 5 seconds to delete the imported copy.
The imported copy was deleted. Saves are kept.
A statically recompiled game, run by XRecomp (the xboxrecomp runtime) on Android arm64. No game data is included: the app reads the copy you set up from a disc you own.
Not affiliated with or endorsed by the console\'s or the game\'s makers. Use only games you own.
Not enough internal storage to prepare the game: %1$s needed, %2$s free.
This device has %1$s of memory: preparing may be slow or fail (6 GB or more recommended).
You can leave the app: it carries on in the background.
Stops now; what is done is kept for next time
Press again to cancel the preparation.
The preparation was cancelled. What was done is kept: Resume carries on from there.
The preparation was interrupted (the system closed it). What was done is kept: Prepare carries on from there.
The system stopped the compiler twice (not enough memory, or Android\'s limit on background processes). Close other apps and retry.
Internal storage is full (%1$s free). Free some space, then retry: what was done is kept.
prepare.log, to you or a developer
No app on this device can receive the log.
Progress of the game\'s preparation, with Cancel
Ready: open the app and press Play.
The preparation failed (%1$s). Open the app to see why.
In the game, Back opens the game menu (settings, quit). Saves stay on this device.
Made once, here on the device, from your own copy: then Play starts at once.
Preparing your game. You can leave the app: it carries on in the background.
The preparation stopped on an error. See why, then retry from where it stopped.
A disc folder or a disc image
Then retry from where it stopped
Short sounds when you move and select

On: a soft tick when the selection moves or a value changes, and short sounds to select, go back, for an error and when the game is ready. Off: the launcher is silent. The game\'s own sound is not affected.
A light buzz with each move and press
On: the device gives a light buzz when the selection moves, a press, an error and when the game is ready. Android\'s own « touch feedback » setting must be on too. Off: no buzz from the launcher.
Only the launcher\'s screens; saved at once.

Panel: the game\'s card and buttons here, and in the game the Xbox buttons the device lacks (Black, White, Back, Start) and a few tools. Black: the second screen stays black. Off: the app leaves it to the system.
The same for any gamepad Android sees: the game reads it as the first Xbox controller. Buttons are taken by position, as Android names them.
